payload.title: How to Get Married in the Seychelles
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, who have the Seychelles on the shortlist and want to know, before they commit to a resort or an island, whether a Seychelles ceremony is legally binding for them, which documents to gather first and what the Civil Status Office asks of them in what order, how to make the certificate count back in Australia, and whether Mahé, Praslin or La Digue suits the wedding they picture. They want one calm, authoritative sequence, not a resort package list.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation (speak with a Wedded Advisor) at /wonderland-concierge.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'getting married in seychelles' are led by resort and package sellers and generic island listicles, with the legal side either thin, undated or copied between pages. This guide is written for Australians and in the order they have to act: whether they can marry legally in the Seychelles, only as official Seychelles sources state; documents first, then entry; the Civil Status Office process step by step exactly as its official pages state it; then the part resort pages skip, getting the certificate ready for Australia (Apostille and recognition, linked to our expert-advice pages); beach and resort ceremonies only as sourced, otherwise the questions a private, high-budget couple should put to a resort (exclusive use, security, privacy, deposits, step-free access); weather from the Seychelles Meteorological Authority by station with seasons as stated; and a business-free chooser across Mahé, Praslin and La Digue from the Seychelles Tourism Board. Figure-free, dated once as at November 2026, third in the 'Getting Married in {Country}' series.
outline_spine: Intro: direct answer in the first 100 words (Australians can marry legally in the Seychelles by following the Civil Status Office process, as officially stated; this guide takes it step by step), then exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways.
Can Australians marry legally in the Seychelles? Civil ceremony and any religious ceremony only as official sources state; legal points dated once as at November 2026.

Documents first, then entry: documents the Civil Status Office asks for (CNI or translation only if stated), then entry from Smartraveller Seychelles and official Seychelles entry pages; no amounts or processing times.

Step by step with the Seychelles Civil Status Office: application, any notice or waiting rules, appearances, who performs the ceremony, witnesses, registration and certificate copies; every step only as official pages state it; 'a fee applies' only where stated.
Getting your certificate ready for Australia: Apostille (Seychelles issuing body as sourced), translation if relevant, recognition back home (Smartraveller, AGD); link the four expert-advice pages.

Beach and resort ceremonies: only what an official source states; otherwise questions to put to the resort on exclusive use, security, privacy, deposits and step-free access, and whether the officer attends on site; packages only as a question to ask.
When to marry: Seychelles Meteorological Authority climate figures labelled by station; seasons only as officially stated; no best month.
Choose your island: Mahé, Praslin and La Digue, one or two lines each from the Seychelles Tourism Board; no businesses, no ranking.
Venues and planning: one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts.md (primary CTA); /magazine once; never legal paperwork help.
Close: plan your Seychelles wedding with a Wedded Advisor (closing CTA).
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words that Australians can marry legally in the Seychelles by following the Civil Status Office process as officially stated.
Exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one concise sentence, no figures, no prices.
The section spine above as H2s in sentence case, matching the series template order, no pasted or bracketed keywords.

Civil Status Office steps, documents, notice or waiting rules, officer, witnesses, registration and certificate copies only as official Seychelles pages state them; 'as at November 2026' used once for legal points.

Australian recognition section linking /expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one, /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home, /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate and /expert-advice/what-is-a-certificate-of-no-impediment-and-who-issues-it; never state the Seychelles requires a CNI unless an official source says so.
Resort questions on exclusive use, security, privacy, deposits and step-free access where no official beach or resort rule is sourced.
Weather from the Seychelles Meteorological Authority labelled by station; island lines for Mahé, Praslin and La Digue only from the Seychelles Tourism Board.

One Wedded Advisor line in the body plus the close, claims only from brand-facts.md 'Claims we can make' (single point of contact, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, fee agreed in writing before work begins, inclusions confirmed in writing); /magazine once; series sisters /destination-weddings/mauritius-wedding and /destination-weddings/getting-married-in-hawaii linked once each.
avoid: Any price, fee amount, SCR, USD or AUD figure, 'from' price, percentage or processing time, including FAQ, meta and takeaways.
Packages described as offers or inclusions; packages appear only as a question to ask the resort.
'Best' anywhere (best island, best month, best resort).
Any statement of the legal position for same-sex couples.
Any Advisor or Wedded Wonderland role in legal paperwork, Civil Status Office applications, apostilles, translations or registration.
Wedded Privileges, room blocks, transfers, 'free', availability promises.
Resort, venue, vendor, officiant, ferry or planner names and any business or contact details (deferred).
Beach or public-land ceremony rules not traced to an official page.
Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, sources or method); hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, resort or package sellers, directories, forums or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images (including Easy Weddings).
US spelling, em dashes, exclamation marks, cliches, 'last dance'.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.

key_takeaways_plan: Australians can have a legally binding wedding in the Seychelles by following the Civil Status Office process as it stands.
Gather your documents first, then check entry requirements, using only official Seychelles and Australian government guidance.
Get your marriage certificate apostilled so the marriage is ready to use back in Australia.
Choose your island and season from official tourism and weather sources, and ask your resort how a beach ceremony, privacy and exclusive use work before you book.
